statement: I did not author this candidate. I inspected its captured patch, isolated summary implementation and regression source, frozen claim/probe, and the two raw receipts used as frozen input fixtures. Those input receipts are not candidate-runtime results. No candidate runtime result was seen and no candidate execution, test, or proof was performed.

findings.assessment: No blocking defect found for the selected fully qualified receipt paths. Real receipt repo fields are canonical absolute paths. Windows drive-qualified and backslash-UNC roots select path.win32; POSIX roots select path.posix. The same selected dialect is consistently used for claim relativization, origin separator normalization, direct absolute command arguments, and --option=absolute-path arguments. Receipt-file lookup still correctly uses the reviewing host's own filesystem semantics.

The frozen probe invokes the actual snapshot CLI summary command on genuine stored-receipt fixtures and checks structured output while preserving digest and revision identities. Hard-coded regression expectations independently cover drive paths, same-share UNC paths, cross-drive volume fallback, and POSIX paths. Literal observations are explicitly checked to remain unchanged; this is structured path presentation, not a general private-data scrubber. Static reasoning predicts the Linux behavioral claim will verify.

The reviewed claim and fixtures use fully qualified paths. Rooted-but-drive-less Windows argv such as \cache, drive-relative arguments, and shell slash-options are not covered by this trial. Their contextual meaning is not established merely by selecting path.win32, and Node resolution of incomplete paths can retain host/current-directory context. The change should not be described as arbitrary-command redaction or complete portability for every possible argv spelling. This does not block the selected canonical-path defect fix.
